subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should OpenClaw expose a public synchronous plugin-facing config pre-apply veto for persisted config writes, and what ordering and failure semantics should it have?
rationale: This would define a public plugin API around config, auth, provider, and secret-adjacent writes, so automation should not choose fail-open/fail-closed policy, hook ordering, redaction, timeout, recursion, or actor-metadata semantics on its own.

options.title: Design the hook contract first
options.body: Specify the typed event, changed-path metadata, SecretRef/redaction ordering, failure policy, timeout behavior, and shared-helper coverage before implementation.

options.title: Fold into the broader preflight framework
options.body: Keep this issue open but resolve it through the wider config validation/preflight design if that work will also cover mandatory pre-persistence plugin vetoes.

options.title: Reject plugin vetoes
options.body: Close this as intentionally unsupported and rely on built-in validation, doctor fixes, and the agent-tool allowlist instead of allowing plugins to block config writes.

recommendation.title: Design the hook contract first
recommendation.body: Specify the typed event, changed-path metadata, SecretRef/redaction ordering, failure policy, timeout behavior, and shared-helper coverage before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already gave the issue-level product-routing review and tied the request to the config validation/mutation RFC direction.
